answer.book: Ramondou's Philosophia naturalis (Venice, 1667), a Latin course in natural philosophy: dedication, preface and prelude, then four parts; the first gives the eight books of the Physics, each split into disputations and disquisitions with unnumbered conclusions, and the others cover the world, animate bodies and metaphysics.
